warnings: Vitamin E from supplements and fortified foods should stay below 300 mg alpha-tocopherol per day for adults (EFSA 2024); 1000 mg per day is the US upper limit for supplements.
Vitamin E from ordinary food does not count toward the upper limit concern.

People taking blood thinners (e.g. warfarin) or antiplatelet medicines (e.g. aspirin, clopidogrel), with a bleeding disorder or vitamin K deficiency, or before surgery should not take vitamin E supplements unless a doctor advises it.

High-dose vitamin E supplements have not prevented heart disease or cancer in large trials; 400 IU per day slightly raised prostate cancer risk in healthy men (SELECT) and heart failure in people with vascular disease or diabetes (HOPE-TOO).
Antioxidant supplements may reduce the benefit of statin plus niacin treatment and may interact with cancer treatment; ask the treating doctor.
Indian 400 mg tocopheryl acetate capsules may equal 180-364 mg alpha-tocopherol depending on whether the form is synthetic or natural.
Pregnancy: take vitamin E supplements only if prescribed.
General information, not medical advice. Check with a doctor before starting supplements.
